This is a review/overview article summarizing the pharmacology and efficacy of amisulpride, not a randomised controlled trial. It describes general findings from multiple studies rather than presenting original RCT data.

This study describes the development and validation of a rating scale for akathisia. While it mentions schizophrenic inpatients, it does not involve amisulpride as an intervention and is not an RCT comparing treatments.

This is a multicentre, double-blind, flexible-dose RCT comparing amisulpride (400-1200 mg/d) to haloperidol (10-30 mg/d, a typical antipsychotic) in 199 patients with paranoid schizophrenia or schizophreniform disorders. Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, amisulpride vs typical antipsychotic, schizophrenia population.
This study describes the development of psychiatric assessment scales for chronic psychotic patients. It is not an intervention study involving amisulpride and does not meet the RCT criterion.

This is a parallel-group, double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT comparing amisulpride (100 mg/d and 300 mg/d) to placebo in 104 in-patients with schizophrenia (DSM-III criteria). Meets all selection criteria: RCT design, amisulpride vs placebo, schizophrenia population.

This is a review article summarizing published clinical experience with atypical neuroleptics in children and adolescents. While it mentions amisulpride among several drugs reviewed, it is not an original RCT.

While this is a randomized, double-blind, crossover trial involving amisulpride in children with autism (which could be considered a non-affective serious mental illness), the comparator is bromocriptine (a dopamine agonist), not placebo or an antipsychotic drug. Does not meet the selection criteria requiring comparison to placebo, typical, or atypical antipsychotics.

This is described as an \'open trial\' (not blinded) where patients on stable haloperidol were randomized to adjunctive amisulpride or fluoxetine. While it involves amisulpride in schizophrenia, the comparator is fluoxetine (an antidepressant), not placebo or another antipsychotic. Additionally, the open-label design raises concerns about bias.
This study is about airway resistance measurement in respiratory medicine, completely unrelated to amisulpride, schizophrenia, or antipsychotic drugs. Clearly does not meet any selection criteria.

This study describes the modification and validation of a rating scale for extrapyramidal side effects. While relevant to antipsychotic research, it is not an intervention study involving amisulpride and does not meet the RCT criterion.

This is described as an \'open clinical study\' (not randomized or blinded). The abstract only mentions pharmacological screening findings without describing a controlled trial design. Does not meet the RCT criterion.
